question: Solve for $x$ and $y$ simultaneously: $$x - 2y = -3 \quad \text{and} \quad xy = 20$$
memo: $$\begin{aligned} x &= 2y - 3 \quad \dots (1) \\ xy &= 20 \quad \dots (2) \end{aligned}$$ Substitute (1) into (2): $$\begin{aligned} (2y - 3)y &= 20 \\ 2y^2 - 3y - 20 &= 0 \\ (2y + 5)(y - 4) &= 0 \\ y = -\frac{5}{2} \quad &\text{or} \quad y = 4 \\ x = -8 \quad &\text{or} \quad x = 5 \end{aligned}$$ * $\checkmark$ making $x$ the subject / maak $x$ die o/w * $\checkmark$ substitution * $\checkmark$ standard form / stand vorm * $\checkmark$ factors / faktore * $\checkmark$ $y$-values / wrdes * $\checkmark$ $x$-values / wrdes

question: Bewys dat die eerste verskille van hierdie patroon altyd onewe sal wees.
memo:
$T_n = an^2 + bn + c$
$2a = 6 \Rightarrow a = 3$
$3(a) + b = 7 \Rightarrow 3(3) + b = 7 \Rightarrow b = -2$
$a + b + c = 5 \Rightarrow 3 - 2 + c = 5 \Rightarrow c = 4$
$T_n = 3n^2 - 2n + 4$
Eerste verskille: $T_{n+1} - T_n = [3(n+1)^2 - 2(n+1) + 4] - [3n^2 - 2n + 4]$
$= 3n^2 + 6n + 3 - 2n - 2 + 4 - 3n^2 + 2n - 4$
$= 6n + 1$
Om te bewys dat $6n + 1$ altyd onewe is: $2(3n) + 1$, wat altyd onewe is vir alle natuurlike getalle $n$.

memo:
Axis of symmetry with negative gradient is $y = -x - 1$.
Intersection with $f$ closest to $A$:
$-x - 1 = \dfrac{-9}{x-1} - 2$ $\checkmark$
$-x + 1 = \dfrac{-9}{x-1}$
$-(x - 1) = \dfrac{-9}{x-1}$
$(x - 1)^2 = 9$ $\checkmark$
$x - 1 = 3$ or $x - 1 = -3$
$x = 4$ or $x = -2$
For the fourth quadrant (since $x > 1$): $x = 4$ $\checkmark$
If $x = 4$, $y = -(4) - 1 = -5$ $\checkmark$
Coordinates: $(4; -5)$ $\checkmark$

question: Bewys dat die verdienste van 'n inkomste van minder as $\text{R}3\ 200$ per maand nie onafhanklik is van die gebied waarin 'n persoon woon nie.
memo: Toets vir onafhanklikheid: $P(< \text{R}3\ 200) \times P(\text{Gebied } 2) = P(< \text{R}3\ 200 \text{ en Gebied } 2)$\\ $P(< \text{R}3\ 200) = \frac{960}{2\ 646} = \frac{160}{441} \approx 0,3628$\\ $P(\text{Gebied } 2) = \frac{814}{2\ 646} = \frac{407}{1\ 323} \approx 0,3077$\\ $P(< \text{R}3\ 200) \times P(\text{Gebied } 2) = \frac{160}{441} \times \frac{407}{1\ 323} = \frac{65\ 120}{583\ 443} \approx 0,1116$\\ $P(< \text{R}3\ 200 \text{ en Gebied } 2) = \frac{460}{2\ 646} = \frac{230}{1\ 323} \approx 0,1738$\\ Omdat $\frac{65\ 120}{583\ 443} \neq \frac{230}{1\ 323}$ ($0,1116 \neq 0,1738$), is die gebeurtenisse nie onafhanklik nie.
final_answer: $P(< \text{R}3\ 200) \times P(\text{Gebied } 2) \neq P(< \text{R}3\ 200 \text{ en Gebied } 2)$, dus is dit nie onafhanklik nie.
